design_decisions: SetComponentProperty was not used. Despite its JsonValue parameter name it calls FProperty::ImportText, wants Unreal text format, and discards the parse result. Component properties marshal through FJsonObjectConverter instead, the same call ReadObjectPropertyJson and SetObjectPropertyJson use, so one marshaling story covers the whole reflection lane.

UObject references are resolved by explicit LoadObject rather than left to the converter. Verified in 4.27 engine source first: JsonObjectConverter.cpp line 726 sends an FObjectProperty string to FProperty::ImportText, and FObjectPropertyBase::ImportText_Internal (PropertyBaseObject.cpp line 346) ignores its own bOk, setting the property to null and returning a non-null buffer. FindImportedObject does load a fully qualified path, so the happy path would have worked, but an unresolvable path would have applied nothing and reported success. That is the exact failure this tool exists to make visible.

The JSON value's shape is checked against the property category before the converter runs. The same discarded-ImportText fallback covers every other type, and probing caught two live cases: "RelativeScale3D": "big" was accepted and wrote nothing, and "Mobility": 7.5 wrote an out-of-range enumerator that tripped an engine ensure inside USceneComponent::PostEditChangeProperty. A struct now requires an object, an array an array, a number a number, an enum a real enumerator by name or value. The table is narrow on purpose: a property category not named there still goes to the converter.

Property checks run in the existing validate-before-mutate pass, so a bad property name or asset path rejects the whole spec before an asset is created. The apply pass still reports its own failures as structured errors, which set success false through the runtime's errors.length gate, so a rerun after a fix converges.

The writable-property allowlist that governs set_property on level actors is not consulted. It is eight entries long and would reject StaticMesh outright. The boundary for authoring is the /Game/MCPGenerated/ asset-path limit blueprint_build already enforced.
Properties are applied to existing components too, not only newly created ones, because a rerun with a changed value has to converge on the new value.
Errors name component, property, and reason in one sentence, including the array element index, so a caller can find the entry in its own spec.

build_and_verify.cpp_build_detail: Build.bat UE427PuerTSMCPEditor Win64 Development, zero errors each time: 8 actions / 13.0 s for the first cut, then 4 actions / 7.2 s for the shape check, then 4 actions / 7.4 s for the enum range check. The two extra cycles are the two silent-no-op holes probing found after the first build; each needed the editor stopped, the file copied to the test project, and a restart.

notes: The two follow-up C++ cycles are the interesting part of this chunk. The first cut applied properties correctly and passed its acceptance; probing invalid values afterwards is what found that FJsonObjectConverter answers success for values it cannot honour. Both holes are engine behaviour, not bridge behaviour, and both are now rejected before an asset is touched.

The Mobility 7.5 probe created /Game/MCPGenerated/BP_ProbeProps before the fix landed. It was deleted from disk while the editor was stopped for the next rebuild, so /Game/MCPGenerated ends with the same three assets it started with.

Changing a component template does not update instances already in the level; the compile does not re-run construction on them. Recorded as limitation 6 in its new form. A probe actor has to be respawned to show a template change.
Every blueprint_build save still logs 'Unable to Check Out From Source Control' as an auto-dismissed modal. The save succeeds; the test project has a source control provider it cannot reach.

puerts-runtime/src/registry.ts needed no change: objectArray passes each component object through untouched, and the runtime's success gate is already errors.length === 0, so an apply-time property error reports success false without new code.
puerts-runtime/typing/ue/ue.d.ts was not regenerated; it is an editor-toolbar snapshot and the runtime compiles against the hand-written puerts-bootstrap.d.ts, which needed no new declaration.
recommended_next_goal: Phase F2: a Blueprint actor with variables and a real event graph. The blocker is the node vocabulary (limitation 8): BuildBlueprintFromJSON has eight node types and no variables, loops, or timers. UBlueprintMutatorLibrary is the richer surface to re-front next.
